title: Guan Yu's Bone-Scraping Surgery: Was the Doctor Really Hua Tuo?
description: Guan Yu playing a board game with Ma Liang while Hua Tuo scrapes his bone: how does that scene differ from the old left-arm wound and the unnamed doctor recorded in Chen Shou's Records of the Three Kingdoms? This episode checks the Biography of Guan Yu, the Biography of Hua Tuo, the Biography of Cao Chong and chapter 75 of the Romance of the Three Kingdoms one by one. The novel's Hua Tuo scene at Fancheng does not fit the historical timeline; for the undated treatment in the history, who the doctor was still cannot be settled. The images are cartoon illustrations, not footage of the historical scene. Information as of 2026-10-19.

chapters.gs001: A doctor gives his name in a tent at Fancheng
chapters.gs007: An arrow at Fancheng; a boat brings a man calling himself Hua Tuo
chapters.gs022: Chen Shou records Guan Yu's old left-arm wound
chapters.gs045: Hua Tuo is killed; Cao Cao later grieves over Cao Chong

gs001.text: In the Romance, Guan Yu and Ma Liang play a game in a Fancheng tent; a doctor with medicines arrives.

gs002.text: He'd already told Guan Ping his name: surname Hua, given name Tuo, courtesy name Yuanhua.

gs003.text: Is the wounded arm in that tent the one Chen Shou recorded?

gs004.text: But if we add the year of Fancheng, could this doctor make it?

gs005.text: Did the doctor in the history leave a name?

gs006.text: Rescuing his father, Guan Ping pulls an arrow from his arm.

gs007.text: The novel puts this wound at Fancheng: an arrow in his right arm.

gs008.text: The arrowhead carried poison, it adds; the arm swelled blue-green and could barely move.

gs009.text: Fearing for his arm, Guan Ping urges rest in Jingzhou.

gs010.text: Fancheng is so close; Guan Yu won't retreat over one arrow. Where will his men get a doctor?

gs011.text: One day a boat comes from Jiangdong; a man aboard has a green medicine bag.

gs012.text: The doctor who gave Guan Ping his name says he's from Qiao in Pei, come on hearing of the poisoned arrow.

gs101.text: Guan Ping asks if he's the Hua Tuo who treated Zhou Tai; in the novel, he says yes.

gs013.text: Guan Ping leads him to the tent with the game; only then do the two meet.

gs014.text: Guan Yu holds out his right arm. What cure will he hear?

gs015.text: Hua Tuo says an aconite crossbow bolt reached the bone; untreated, the arm may be lost.

gs016.text: He'd tie the arm to a pillar ring, cover the head, cut, scrape out the poison, dress and stitch it.

gs017.text: Guan Yu laughs off the restraints and simply holds out his arm. Can he stay this calm the whole time?

gs018.text: Wine is served; the game and the surgery go on together.

gs117.text: An officer holds a big basin for the blood. What does the history say?

gs019.text: As the blade cuts, onlookers go pale; Guan Yu eats and drinks as usual.

gs113.text: Hua Tuo even says he's never seen so calm a patient in his life.

gs102.text: Guan Yu flexes his right arm and calls him a divine physician. What does the doctor warn?

gs111.text: At the thank-you feast Hua Tuo warns: the wound is treated, but guard it; don't strain it in anger.

gs112.text: He says it will heal in a hundred days. Guan Yu offers 100 taels of gold.

gs105.text: Hua Tuo refuses, leaves a dose of medicine and goes; the novel sees him all the way out.

gs020.text: How does Guan Yu's biography open this wound?

gs022.text: It says a "stray arrow" hit Guan Yu; no doctor walks into a tent.

gs116.text: It never says who shot it, but it says which arm was hurt.

gs023.text: The word "once" puts it in the past; it doesn't pin it to a Fancheng tent.

gs024.text: It pierced the left arm, not the right.

gs025.text: The wound healed, but the bone ached whenever it rained. How would a doctor treat that old pain?

gs104.text: Both scrape the bone, but the visit starts differently; the novel's later details can't fill the biography.

gs026.text: This doctor also says the arrowhead's poison reached the bone, but gives it no name.

gs027.text: This is an ancient biography relaying a doctor's view; "poisoned" isn't a modern lab result.

gs028.text: He says: open the arm, scrape the bone, end the pain.

gs029.text: Guan Yu holds out his left arm at once; no pillar ring, no covered head. Who was with him?

gs119.text: The novel had an officer hold the basin; Guan Yu's biography has a dish full of blood too. Now, who's beside him?

gs030.text: It says he was hosting his generals; no Ma Liang, no game.

gs031.text: Before his generals he cut meat and raised his cup as usual, talking and laughing.

gs032.text: So far, can you find the doctor's name?

gs033.text: No. The biography lets the doctor speak, but never gives his name.

gs037.text: So which year does the history give for the surgery?

gs038.text: No date for the visit here; no date or season for the surgery.

gs039.text: Only in the next passage does Chen Shou write "the 24th year."

gs106.text: That year Liu Bei became King of Hanzhong and made Guan Yu General of the Front; that's dated too.

gs040.text: That's the 24th year of Jian'an, or 219 AD.

gs041.text: That year Guan Yu besieged Fancheng, held by Cao Ren. Can that clear date also fix the earlier treatment?

gs120.text: It also has heavy autumn rain and the Han River in flood; Fancheng has a clearer time and place than the surgery.

gs121.text: But the text never says the old wound's rain was this flood; drawing both rains as one scene goes beyond the text.

gs043.text: Lending that date to the surgery makes certain what the text never said.

gs044.text: Yet the novel puts the doctor at Fancheng's front. What does the timeline say?

gs045.text: Hua Tuo's biography gives no exact date of death, but ties it to another person's illness.

gs046.text: Cao Cao fell gravely ill and wanted Hua Tuo all to himself; Hua Tuo went home, citing a sick wife. What did Cao do?

gs047.text: He summoned him again and again, had the illness checked, and finally jailed him in Xu.

gs048.text: Xun Yu urged him to spare a doctor whose skill saved lives; Cao Cao refused.

gs107.text: Then the biography sums up Hua Tuo's end in four characters. Which ones?

gs049.text: It reads "sui kao jing Tuo": in the end, Hua Tuo was put to death.

gs050.text: Cao Cao's headaches outlived Hua Tuo. How had he justified killing him?

gs114.text: Cao Cao said Hua Tuo could cure him but kept the illness to seem vital; that's only Cao Cao's charge.

gs115.text: But when someone else lay dying, that excuse turned to regret. Who was it?

gs051.text: When his beloved son Cangshu fell gravely ill, Cao Cao rued killing Hua Tuo.

gs052.text: Who was Cangshu? How does his illness fence in the year Hua Tuo died?

gs053.text: Cao Chong's biography: Cao Chong, styled Cangshu.

gs054.text: It says Cao Chong died of illness at thirteen, in the 13th year of Jian'an. What year is that?

gs108.text: It also says Cao Cao grieved for the boy, weeping as he spoke.

gs056.text: Hua Tuo's biography says "after Tuo died" before Cao Chong's illness, so Hua Tuo died before the boy.

gs057.text: With that line drawn, can the Romance's doctor at Fancheng still make it?

gs058.text: The Fancheng campaign came 11 years after Cao Chong died.

gs059.text: By this timeline, the novel's Hua Tuo can't reach Fancheng in time.

gs062.text: If the historical left-arm surgery was earlier, can the timeline alone exclude Hua Tuo?

gs063.text: No; it doesn't list everyone Hua Tuo treated in his lifetime.

gs065.text: Hua Tuo's biography lists many patients, but not Guan Yu's left arm.

gs066.text: So what evidence is missing to give this doctor a name?

gs067.text: A reliable record clearly tied to this left-arm surgery; the novel's self-introduction is another genre.

gs069.text: Put the novel's game and the history's surgery together. Where does it go wrong?

gs071.text: A picture of the game should be credited to chapter 75 of the Romance, not to Chen Shou's biography of Guan Yu.

gs118.text: The novel only says "played a game", never the board or pieces; props in a picture can't testify for the text.

gs074.text: When you picture Guan Yu's bone scraping, is it a dinner table or a game board?
